object.dateLabel: 22 December 1808 (premiere, Theater an der Wien); composed 1804-1808
object.medium: Symphony for orchestra; autograph score, ink on paper
object.description: Beethoven worked on his Fifth Symphony between 1804 and 1808, in the years when his deafness was becoming impossible to hide. It was first played on 22 December 1808 at the Theater an der Wien in Vienna, in a freezing hall, as part of a four-hour concert of his new music. The opening, three short notes and a long one hammered out by the whole orchestra, is the most famous beginning in music, and the symphony's journey from that C minor storm to a blazing C major finale with trombones and piccolo became the model for a century of symphonies that end in triumph. The page shown is the first leaf of Beethoven's own manuscript, kept at the Berlin State Library. The visitor hears the first movement, Allegro con brio, played by the Fulda Symphonic Orchestra under Simon Schindler in a 2002 recording the orchestra released into the public domain.
facts: The 1808 premiere concert also introduced the Sixth Symphony, the Fourth Piano Concerto and the Choral Fantasy, with Beethoven himself at the piano.
Beethoven's secretary Anton Schindler claimed the composer said of the opening, 'Thus Fate knocks at the door', a story most scholars doubt.
The autograph score is one of the treasures of the Staatsbibliothek zu Berlin, which has digitised it page by page.
